requirements.text: The Files header shows both the context the explorer is following and the current folder's name: the app's name for an app root, 'Misc' for a loose file's folder, or 'Home' for the user's home folder, together with the folder name it shows today.

The Projects tab label carries one status dot that rolls up all apps' executable terminals using the existing roll-up rules (red if any failed, green if all up, amber if some up or stopping, grey otherwise), and the rail's Projects icon shows the same dot where the existing rail style allows; the label still reads clearly with the dot.

The active sidebar tab is kept for the running session only: the app starts on Projects every time it opens, the tab chosen by a tab click, a rail icon or the shortcut is remembered while the app runs, and expanding after a collapse shows the tab that was active before collapsing. No new layout value is saved; 'td.sidebarCollapsed' remains the only saved sidebar layout value.

Pressing Ctrl+Shift+E shows the Files tab, expanding the sidebar first when it is collapsed; the shortcut is added to the single shared app-shortcut list so the command palette and help list it, and a focused terminal hands the combination to the app instead of the shell.
Switching away from the Files tab and back returns to the folder and expanded levels the user was viewing; a tab switch does not reset the explorer's navigation or scroll.
